title: The Claws of a Bear Market

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报《DealBook》的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于 NYTimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: There are new fears of a recession after a miserable start to the week on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 华尔街本周遭遇悲惨开局后，人们对经济衰退产生了新的担忧。

sentences.en: Stocks plunged Monday across the board.
sentences.zh: 周一股市全面暴跌。

sentences.en: Why the United States stock market has been plunging.
sentences.zh: 为什么美国股市一直在暴跌。

sentences.en: Economists are tossing around a term you don't hear every day.
sentences.zh: 经济学家们正在频频抛出一个你平时不常听到的词。

sentences.en: A bear market.
sentences.zh: 熊市。

sentences.en: A bear market.
sentences.zh: 熊市。

sentences.en: We're looking at a bear market.
sentences.zh: 我们正在经历熊市。

sentences.en: And what it reveals about growing fears that what's required to fix the economy will end up pushing it into a recession.
sentences.zh: 这折射出人们日益担忧：修复经济所需的举措最终会将其推入衰退。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Jim Tankersley, Wednesday, June 15th.
sentences.zh: 6月15日星期三，我采访了我的同事吉姆·坦克雷斯利。

sentences.en: And we are solidly in bear market territory.
sentences.zh: 我们现在确确实实处于熊市区间。

sentences.en: So, Jim, a bear market.
sentences.zh: 那么，吉姆，熊市。

sentences.en: Why is it called a bear market?
sentences.zh: 为什么它被称为熊市？

sentences.en: I want to begin with some trivia.
sentences.zh: 我想从一些冷知识开始说起。

sentences.en: Well, no one for sure knows, but there are some theories.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有人确切知道，但有一些理论。

sentences.en: At least this is what, reading up on it, this is what I have learned.
sentences.zh: 至少根据我的阅读，这就是我所了解到的。

sentences.en: The predominant theory is about the way animals attack.
sentences.zh: 主流的理论与动物的攻击方式有关。

sentences.en: When animals attack, stock market version.
sentences.zh: 当动物攻击时，股市版本。

sentences.en: So, the theory about when animals attack is that bulls, a bull market is a positive market when stocks go up.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于动物攻击的理论是，牛——牛市是指股票上涨的积极市场。

sentences.en: They attack with their horns sweeping up.
sentences.zh: 它们的角是向上挥舞进行攻击的。

sentences.en: But bears attack with their claws sweeping downward.
sentences.zh: 但熊是用爪子向下挥舞攻击的。

sentences.en: So, a bear market is when the stocks go down.
sentences.zh: 因此，熊市就是股票下跌的时候。

sentences.en: Right, because a bear's claws pull the prey down.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为熊的爪子把猎物往下按。

sentences.en: It's all about bear claws.
sentences.zh: 这全跟熊爪有关。

sentences.en: It's a bear claw...
sentences.zh: 这是一种熊爪……

sentences.en: ...kind of market.
sentences.zh: ……式的市场。

sentences.en: ...kind of market.
sentences.zh: ……式的市场。

sentences.en: Okay, and the bear market is the bad market.
sentences.zh: 好的，熊市就是糟糕的市场。

sentences.en: What defines a bear market, technically speaking?
sentences.zh: 从技术层面上讲，什么定义了熊市？

sentences.en: It's when stocks have fallen 20% from a recent peak.
sentences.zh: 就是股票从近期高点下跌了20%。

sentences.en: So, they rise to a certain level, they level off, and then they fall.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们上涨到一定水平，趋于平稳，然后下跌。

sentences.en: And if they fall 20% or more, that is technically a bear market.
sentences.zh: 如果它们下跌20%或更多，在技术上这就是一个熊市。

sentences.en: And, you know, for practical purposes, quite bad for investors.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，从实际角度来看，这对投资者来说相当糟糕。

sentences.en: And just explain that when we say quite bad for investors.
sentences.zh: 给我们解释一下，当我们说对投资者相当糟糕时这意味着什么。

sentences.en: Well, it means a lot of companies are seeing their stock prices decline rather precipitously.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这意味着许多公司的股价正在相当急剧地下降。

sentences.en: It means just enormous amounts of money, of corporate value being erased on paper anyway, at least temporarily.
sentences.zh: 这意味着巨额的资金、企业价值正在纸面上被抹去，至少暂时是这样。

sentences.en: And it means that, you know, if you are someone who has your savings in stocks, and you rely upon those for your retirement or something else,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，你知道，如果你把积蓄存放在股票中，并且依靠这些来过退休生活或其他事情，

sentences.en: and you suddenly need to get money out right now, well, you're down.
sentences.zh: 而你突然现在就需要把钱取出来，好吧，你亏了。

sentences.en: You're down a lot from where you would have been if you had sold or been taking money out at the top of the market.
sentences.zh: 相比于你在市场顶峰时卖出或取钱的情况，你现在缩水了很多。

sentences.en: So, it has real-world effects on a lot of people, and real psychological effects on investors, on CEOs, and on economists,
sentences.zh: 因此，这对许多人的现实生活产生了实际影响，对投资者、首席执行官和经济学家产生了真正的心理影响，

sentences.en: and the way that they think about what's happening in the world around us.
sentences.zh: 并影响了他们对周围世界正在发生的事情的看法。

sentences.en: Right, because literally, a few months ago, in this case, you could open up your retirement account, and it would look one way,
sentences.zh: 没错，因为就在几个月前，在这种情况下，你打开退休账户，它看起来是一个样子，

sentences.en: and then now it's one-fifth the value of that, which is a really meaningful decline.
sentences.zh: 而现在它的价值只有当时的五分之一，这是一个非常显著的下跌。

sentences.en: You've lost a fifth of the value off of it, yes, broadly speaking.
sentences.zh: 是的，大体来说，你的资产价值已经缩水了五分之一。

sentences.en: And what's our best understanding of why we have just entered this unfortunate financial territory of a bear market over the past few days?
sentences.zh: 对于我们为什么在过去几天刚刚进入熊市这个不幸的金融领域，我们最好的理解是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the short answer is inflation.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是，通货膨胀。

sentences.en: To back up, we all remember that when the pandemic started, the government gave people a lot of money to help get through the most difficult times of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 回想一下，我们都记得大流行开始时，政府给了人们很多钱，以帮助度过大流行最困难的时期。

sentences.en: People had saved a bunch of that money, and then as the pandemic wore on and the reopening began, people were spending money in different ways.
sentences.zh: 人们存下了一大笔钱，然后随着大流行持续以及经济重新开放，人们开始以不同的方式花钱。

sentences.en: They were buying furniture or other goods, and there was this huge demand, and there weren't enough goods to meet all the demand, and so prices went up, and that created inflation.
sentences.zh: 他们在买家具或其他商品，这里面有巨大的需求，但没有足够的商品来满足所有需求，所以价格上涨了，这就造成了通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And the hope had been that it would be receding by now, that we would have hit a high and it would go down.
sentences.zh: 原本的希望是通胀到现在应该已经开始回落，我们本该触顶然后它会下降。

sentences.en: But instead, we keep getting, month after month, signs that it's at a 40-year high.
sentences.zh: 但相反，我们不断收到一个月又一个月的迹象，表明它正处于40年来的最高点。

sentences.en: For example, last month, we just learned a few days ago, that consumer prices rose 8.6% in May, which is a lot, and a lot more than anyone expected.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们几天前刚刚得知，上个月消费价格在5月份上涨了8.6%，这是一个很大的数字，远超任何人的预期。

sentences.en: And markets are starting to freak out about that.
sentences.zh: 市场开始为此感到恐慌。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And of course, the government has a tool to deal with inflation, which we talked about a lot on the show, which is raising interest rates.
sentences.zh: 当然，政府有一种应对通胀的工具，我们在节目中讨论过很多次，那就是提高利率。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Federal Reserve, which is the central bank, which is charged with keeping inflation at a 2% target, has been signaling that, hey, we're raising interest rates,
sentences.zh: 是的，作为中央银行的联邦储备委员会，其职责是将通胀控制在2%的目标水平，它一直在发出信号，即“嘿，我们要加息了”，

sentences.en: they've started raising interest rates, and signaling that they will continue to raise interest rates in hopes of sort of pulling some spending power out of the economy.
sentences.zh: 他们已经开始加息，并暗示将继续加息，希望以此从经济中抽走一些消费能力。

sentences.en: When rates go up, fewer people can maybe afford a mortgage or afford a car loan, and so they spend less money.
sentences.zh: 当利率上升时，可能负担得起抵押贷款或汽车贷款的人就会减少，因此他们花的钱就会减少。

sentences.en: And that's a way that the Fed controls demand in the economy and brings the price of things down.
sentences.zh: 这是美联储控制经济中需求并压低物价的一种方式。

sentences.en: Right, and Jim, we've talked to our colleague,
sentences.zh: 没错，吉姆，我们和我们的同事吉娜·斯迈利讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: Gina Smiley, about this.
sentences.zh: 这有点复杂，但美联储通过加息实际最终做到的事情是，从某种意义上说，

sentences.en: It's kind of complicated, but what the Federal Reserve actually ends up doing by raising the interest rate is, in some sense,
sentences.zh: 它有点像为了拯救经济而伤害经济。

sentences.en: it kind of hurts the economy in order to help the economy.
sentences.zh: 它必须让许多人借钱和花钱变得稍微困难一些，以便把通货膨胀降下来。

sentences.en: It has to make it a little harder for lots of people to borrow money and spend it in order to bring inflation down.
sentences.zh: 这感觉有悖常理，但这是一个已被证明行之有效的系统。

sentences.en: It feels counterintuitive, but it's a provenly effective system.
sentences.zh: 没错，但这次的问题在于，它还不够有效。

sentences.en: Right, but the problem this time is, it hasn't been effective enough yet.
sentences.zh: 因此，美联储不得不开始谈论以更快的速度加息，这正是市场真正担心的地方。

sentences.en: And so the Fed is having to start talking about raising rates even faster, and that is what markets are really worried about.
sentences.zh: 为什么他们对此如此担心？

sentences.en: And why are they so worried about that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你把刹车踩得太猛，从经济中抽走过多的消费支出，你就有可能把经济推入衰退。

sentences.en: Well, if you pump the brakes too hard, you pull too much consumer spending out of the economy, and you could push the economy into recession.
sentences.zh: 这是许多投资者在这里反映的真正巨大的担忧，即美联储将犯下经济学家所称的政策失误，

sentences.en: That's the really big fear that a lot of investors are reflecting here is that the Fed is going to make what economists call a policy error here
sentences.zh: 行动太快，把经济推下悬崖。

sentences.en: and go too fast and push the economy kind of off a cliff.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 所以投资者的恐惧——这导致他们抛售股票并把股市推入熊市——在于美联储即将对通胀做出过度反应，

sentences.en: So investors' fear, which has led them to sell stock and put the stock market into a bear market, is that the Fed is about to basically overreact to inflation
sentences.zh: 可能过度加息，从而损害经济，将我们送入衰退。

sentences.en: by perhaps overraising interest rates and therefore damage the economy, send us into a recession.
sentences.zh: 没错，甚至可以说，为了降低通胀，美联储面临的通胀问题如此严重，以至于美联储不得不让经济陷入衰退来解决它。

sentences.en: Right, or even that the Fed, in order to get inflation down, the inflation problem is so bad that the Fed is going to have to put the economy in recession to do it.
sentences.zh: 这就好比为了让事情好转，如果我们要扩展这个比喻的话，给病人进行一次短暂的昏迷。

sentences.en: Almost like putting the patient in a coma briefly to try to, if we're going to extend the metaphor, to try to make things better.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你这么做，会产生许多其他非常糟糕的影响。

sentences.en: And so that has a lot of other very bad effects if you do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为投资者反映的是：要么美联储做得太多而弄巧成拙，要么美联储为了驯服通胀必须采取的举措本身，

sentences.en: And so I think investors are reflecting either the Fed's going to do too much and get it wrong or just the amount the Fed has to do to tame inflation
sentences.zh: 就会对经济造成极大的伤害。

sentences.en: is just going to be really bad for the economy.
sentences.zh: 当我们说“衰退”时，继续我们这里的经济学入门系列，我们使用的是一个非常技术的定义，即经济在连续几个季度中收缩而不是增长。

sentences.en: And when we say recession, to continue with our economic 101 series here, we're using this very technical definition of when the economy shrinks rather than grows
sentences.zh: 这不被认为是一件好事。

sentences.en: over a series of quarters.
sentences.zh: 不，这不是好事。

sentences.en: That's not considered a good thing.
sentences.zh: 没有人想要经济衰退。

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 我必须指出，这并不保证我们这次一定会走向衰退。

sentences.en: No one wants a recession.
sentences.zh: 我没有跟任何说我们绝对会走向衰退的经济学家交流过。

sentences.en: And I should just say, there's no guarantee we're headed for one this time.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: I haven't talked to any economist who says we're definitely headed for one.
sentences.zh: 但即使我们真的走向衰退，也有不同类型的衰退。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府内部有些人所认为的大写R衰退（一场相当严重、极其严重的衰退），或者小写r衰退（也许没那么严重）。

sentences.en: But even if we are, there's different types of recessions.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么请帮我们区分一下大写R衰退和小写r衰退。

sentences.en: What some people inside the Biden administration think of as a capital R recession, a pretty bad one, a really bad one, or a small R recession, maybe a less bad one.
sentences.zh: 大写R衰退是我们美国历史上经常经历的那种衰退，一连串的坏事循环发生。

sentences.en: Okay, so help us distinguish between the capital R recession and the lowercase r recession.
sentences.zh: 经济开始收缩。

sentences.en: So the capital R recession is the sort of recession we've experienced a lot in American history where a whole cycle of bad things happens.
sentences.zh: 它没有增长。

sentences.en: The economy starts to contract.
sentences.zh: 它在变小。

sentences.en: It's not growing.
sentences.zh: 因此可流通的资金减少了。

sentences.en: It's getting smaller.
sentences.zh: 去商店、去旅游和花钱的人变少了。

sentences.en: So there's less money to go around.
sentences.zh: 企业不得不裁员。

sentences.en: Fewer people go to shops and go on trips and spend money.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，可能有数百万人会失去工作。

sentences.en: Businesses have to lay people off.
sentences.zh: 失业率飙升。

sentences.en: Millions of people probably in this scenario would lose their jobs.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又让另一大批人可花的钱变少了。

sentences.en: The unemployment rate spikes.
sentences.zh: 于是他们无法购物。

sentences.en: And that in turn gives a whole other batch of people who now have less money to spend.
sentences.zh: 这可能会成为经济活动不断恶化的恶性循环。

sentences.en: And so they can't shop.
sentences.zh: 而且经济可能需要很长时间才能复苏。

sentences.en: And that it just can be a downward spiral of economic activity.
sentences.zh: 这有点像我们在2008年金融危机衰退中所看到的情况。

sentences.en: And it can take a long time to recover from foreign economy.
sentences.zh: 这可能会非常非常具有破坏性，尤其是对处于经济边缘的人、积蓄不多的人、可能被驱逐的人来说，

sentences.en: And this is sort of what we saw in the 2008 financial crisis recession.
sentences.zh: 失去家园，失去工作。

sentences.en: And it can be very, very debilitating for particularly people on the edges of the economy, people with not a lot of money in savings, people who could be evicted,
sentences.zh: 对人们来说，这可能会以非常糟糕的方式改变人生。

sentences.en: lose their homes, lose their jobs.
sentences.zh: 你显然希望避免那样的衰退。

sentences.en: It can be life-changing in a very bad way for people.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you obviously want to avoid a recession like that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们要陷入衰退，那显然不是拜登政府希望我们陷入的那种衰退。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 因为它全方位地糟糕。

sentences.en: That's clearly not the kind of recession if we're going to go into a recession that the Biden administration would want us to be in.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对不是。

sentences.en: Because it's horrible all around.
sentences.zh: 作为一个体验经济生活的人，没有人想要这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 作为一位其命运往往与经济状况紧密相连的总统，没有人想要这个。

sentences.en: Nobody wants that as a person who experiences the economy.
sentences.zh: 如果非得经历衰退不可，拜登政府更倾向于小写r衰退，

sentences.en: Nobody wants that as a president whose fortunes are tied so much often to the state of the economy.
sentences.zh: 对整个经济的影响要温和得多。

sentences.en: The Biden administration would much prefer, if there is going to have to be a recession, they would much prefer sort of the small r recession,
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: much lighter touch across the economy.
sentences.zh: 小写r衰退是什么样的？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 描述一下它的特征。

sentences.en: And what does the lowercase r recession look like?
sentences.zh: 嗯，它始于通货膨胀随着向衰退的转变而下降这一事实。

sentences.en: Describe its characteristics.
sentences.zh: 人们注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: Well, it starts with the fact that inflation comes down as part of this shift into recession.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感觉很好。

sentences.en: And people notice that.
sentences.zh: 经济增长可能会变成负数，但人们可能感觉不到那么多。

sentences.en: They feel good about that.
sentences.zh: 也许只是，从技术上讲，经济在几个季度里收缩了，但感觉并没有真正被猛踩刹车。

sentences.en: Growth maybe turns negative, but maybe people don't feel that as much.
sentences.zh: 没有大规模裁员。

sentences.en: Maybe it's just sort of, technically speaking, the economy is contracting for a few quarters, but it doesn't feel like the brakes have really been slammed.
sentences.zh: 消费活动没有大幅下滑。

sentences.en: There aren't big layoffs.
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，人们只是为了一点：他们的薪水终于赶上了生活成本的上涨，这让他们感觉良好。

sentences.en: There isn't a huge pullback in consumer activity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在最好的情况下，特别是对政府而言，如果你处于边缘地带，

sentences.en: If anything, people are just feeling good about the fact that their salary is keeping up with the rising cost of living, finally.
sentences.zh: 它仍然很有可能对你构成危险并把你置于困境中。

sentences.en: And, you know, in a best case scenario here, particularly for the administration, it's kind of something that if you're on the margins,
sentences.zh: 但对于大多数美国人来说，他们并没有什么太大的感觉。

sentences.en: it very much could still be dangerous for you and put you in a bad spot.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: But for most Americans, they don't feel it that much.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是人们能想象到的最温和的衰退。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this would be as gentle a recession as one could possibly imagine.
sentences.zh: 这是一种理论上的、温和的衰退，对大多数人来说，它只存在于统计数据中。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 在我们的现代历史中，有这种衰退的好例子吗？

sentences.en: This is a sort of theoretical, gentle recession that is sort of a recession in statistics only for most people.
sentences.zh: 没有什么太好的例子。

sentences.en: And is there a good example of this kind of recession in our modern history?
sentences.zh: 大多数时候当我们经历衰退时，失业率都会上升。

sentences.en: There isn't anything great like this.
sentences.zh: 它会大幅上升。

sentences.en: Most of the time when we have recessions, the unemployment rate goes up.
sentences.zh: 这是其中一个重要部分，即失业的人越多，你得到的这些不良连锁反应就越多。

sentences.en: It goes way up.
sentences.zh: 它会一路飙升。

sentences.en: And that's an important part of this is that the more people are thrown out of work, the more that you get these bad knock-on effects.
sentences.zh: 这也是其中很重要的一个部分，那就是失业的人越多，就会产生越多这种糟糕的连锁反应。

sentences.en: We've certainly had short recessions in our modern history.
sentences.zh: 我们在现代历史上确实经历过短暂的经济衰退。

sentences.en: And we've had recessions that economists consider mild, like, for example, coming out of World War II.
sentences.zh: 我们也经历过经济学家认为属于温和的衰退，比如二战结束后的时期。

sentences.en: But even those saw people thrown out of work, and that, again, really is the sort of start of a spiral that can take a while for an economy to recover from.
sentences.zh: 但即使在那些时期，人们也失去了工作，而这再次成为经济需要一段时间才能复苏的恶性循环的开端。

sentences.en: So the Fed and the administration are really trying to thread a needle here.
sentences.zh: 因此，美联储和政府确实在试图走钢丝。

sentences.en: And like I said, we just don't have a lot of examples of that working out the way they want it to.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们并没有太多这样做的结果符合他们预期的先例。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你的第一个月体验是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，享受30天的免费访问权。

sentences.en: So, Jed, just to recap everything you've told us and explain where we are.
sentences.zh: 杰德，为了总结你刚才告诉我们的一切，并解释我们目前的处境。

sentences.en: We're not in a recession, but inflation is really high.
sentences.zh: 我们没有陷入经济衰退，但通货膨胀非常高。

sentences.en: And investors fear the government's plans to lower it by raising interest rates will send us into a recession, which is why we're in a bear market.
sentences.zh: 投资者担心政府通过加息来降低通胀的计划会让我们陷入衰退，这就是我们身处熊市的原因。

sentences.en: How much power does our government, the president, the Federal Reserve, actually have over which version of a recession we enter, if we're going to enter one?
sentences.zh: 我们的政府、总统、美联储，对我们将进入哪种版本的衰退（如果我们真的会进入的话）到底有多大的控制力？

sentences.en: Whether we enter the capital R recession or the lowercase r recession?
sentences.zh: 不管是大写R的经济衰退，还是小写r的经济衰退？

sentences.en: Well, the government has a lot of power, particularly the Fed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，政府拥有很大的权力，尤其是美联储。

sentences.en: And the Fed is kind of constantly searching for the right mix of policies to achieve that result of the lower R recession, or ideally for the Fed, no recession at all,
sentences.zh: 美联储一直在寻找正确的政策组合，以实现那种较低R的经济衰退，或者对美联储来说最理想的、根本没有经济衰退的结果，

sentences.en: a so-called soft landing.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的软着陆。

sentences.en: And so they do.
sentences.zh: 他们的确如此。

sentences.en: They have a lot of power because they are the ones who control interest rate policies.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有很大的权力，因为他们是控制利率政策的人。

sentences.en: It's just not a power that they can necessarily fine-tune to exactly the level they want.
sentences.zh: 只是这种权力不一定能精准调控到他们想要的水平。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's sort of like
sentences.zh: 好的，这有点像

sentences.en: if you're a character in a video game and you can fire a really big fireball or a really small fireball, but you can't fire a medium-sized fireball,
sentences.zh: 如果你是电子游戏里的一个角色，你可以发射一个超级大的火球或者一个超级小的火球，但你无法发射一个中等大小的火球，

sentences.en: that may be what the Fed has here.
sentences.zh: 美联储现在面临的情况可能就是这样。

sentences.en: It can raise interest rates.
sentences.zh: 它可以提高利率。

sentences.en: It can raise them as fast as it wants to.
sentences.zh: 它可以按自己想的速度去提高利率。

sentences.en: It can try to communicate by telling the market, this is the path of interest rate increases that we expect in the future.
sentences.zh: 它可以通过告诉市场来尝试沟通，这就是我们预期的未来加息路径。

sentences.en: It has all of these ways of trying to signal what it's going to do and to generate the response it wants from investors, from consumers, from the broad economy.
sentences.zh: 它拥有所有这些方式来暗示它要做什么，并从投资者、消费者以及整个经济体中引发它想要的反应。

sentences.en: But there's no guarantee that the reaction from the broad economy is going to be exactly what the Fed wants because it's not pulling, you know,
sentences.zh: 但无法保证来自广义经济的反应会完全符合美联储的意愿，因为它拉动的并不是，你知道的，

sentences.en: X amount of demand out of the economy.
sentences.zh: 从经济中抽走特定数量的需求。

sentences.en: It's just trying to bank shot some changes in people's behavior that will produce the outcome it wants.
sentences.zh: 它只是试图通过间接手段改变人们的行为，从而产生它想要的结果。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: For example, I think a lot of us of a certain generation remember, in the 1970s, the Federal Reserve raised the interest rates over and over again
sentences.zh: 例如，我想我们这一代很多人都记得，在20世纪70年代，美联储一次又一次地提高利率

sentences.en: to try to tamp down historically high inflation.
sentences.zh: 来试图压制处于历史高位的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And I'm sure at the time, it looked like their only goal was to tamp down inflation.
sentences.zh: 我确信在当时，他们的唯一目标似乎就是压制通胀。

sentences.en: But in the process, they made borrowing costs so high that people weren't buying houses.
sentences.zh: 但在这一过程中，他们让借贷成本变得如此之高，以至于人们不再买房。

sentences.en: Because people weren't buying houses, people weren't building houses.
sentences.zh: 因为人们不买房，所以人们不建房。

sentences.en: And people weren't building houses, there weren't jobs in the housing industry.
sentences.zh: 因为人们不建房，所以房地产业就没有了工作岗位。

sentences.en: On and on it went.
sentences.zh: 就这样一直持续下去。

sentences.en: And that triggered a really bad economic cycle.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一个非常糟糕的经济周期。

sentences.en: Yeah, actually, we ended up with two recessions right in the early 80s.
sentences.zh: 是的，事实上，我们在80年代初最终迎来了两次经济衰退。

sentences.en: Kind of a quick one right at the start of the 80s and then another one.
sentences.zh: 80年代初刚开始时有一场相当迅速的衰退，然后又是一场。

sentences.en: And yeah, those were both cases where the Fed did what it felt like it needed to do to stop inflation.
sentences.zh: 是的，那两种情况下，美联储都做了它认为必须做的事来制止通胀。

sentences.en: And the result was millions of people losing their jobs, a downward spiral in the economy.
sentences.zh: 结果就是数百万人失去了工作，经济陷入了恶性循环。

sentences.en: Now, the economy recovered.
sentences.zh: 现在，经济复苏了。

sentences.en: That's the good news.
sentences.zh: 这是好消息。

sentences.en: There was roaring growth by the mid-80s.
sentences.zh: 到80年代中期，经济迎来了蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: But boy, it was a hard road to get there.
sentences.zh: 但天哪，走到这一步是一条艰难的路。

sentences.en: And that was definitely a case of the Fed pulling on the brake as hard as it thought it needed to in order to bring inflation down, which it finally did.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是美联储认为有必要死踩刹车以降低通胀的一个例子，它最终也确实做到了。

sentences.en: So, Jim, when you talk to people in the White House, which you do, you are a White House reporter, about how they think this balancing act will play out, raising interest rates
sentences.zh: 吉姆，当你与白宫的人交谈时——你确实会这么做，你是一名白宫记者——关于他们如何看待这种平衡术会如何上演，即加息

sentences.en: but not tipping the economy into a terrible recession, how do they talk about it?
sentences.zh: 但又不会让经济陷入可怕的衰退，他们是怎么谈论这件事的？

sentences.en: Well, it starts with the president.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这一切都从总统开始。

sentences.en: He has made I trust the Federal Reserve to do what is right on inflation his number one talking point on what is the number one economic issue of his presidency right now.
sentences.zh: 他将“我相信美联储会在通胀问题上做出正确的事情”作为他当前总统任期内头号经济议题的最重要谈话要点。

sentences.en: Which is inflation.
sentences.zh: 也就是通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Yeah, right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: The key to his whole strategy is I trust the Fed.
sentences.zh: 他整个战略的关键就是：我相信美联储。

sentences.en: I'm not going to tell them what to do.
sentences.zh: 我不会告诉他们该做什么。

sentences.en: They're independent.
sentences.zh: 他们是独立的。

sentences.en: And I think they're going to get it right.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们会做对的。

sentences.en: So there's a reason for that, not just to show that he's unlike former President Trump, who likes to tell the Fed what to do in public all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以这背后是有原因的，不仅仅是为了表明他不同于前总统特朗普，后者总是喜欢公开对美联储指手画脚。

sentences.en: But it's also the president is trying to signal to the market, to investors like, hey, I think the Fed has this.
sentences.zh: 这也是因为总统正试图向市场和投资者发出信号，比如，嘿，我认为美联储能搞定这个。

sentences.en: So you should take what it's doing as highly credible to arrest inflation.
sentences.zh: 所以你们应该认为它的举措在遏制通胀方面具有高度可信度。

sentences.en: He's hoping to kind of coax that softer landing by getting the market to kind of buy into what the Fed wants.
sentences.zh: 他希望能通过让市场买账美联储的意图，来诱导实现那种更温和的软着陆。

sentences.en: And when administration officials talk about it, that's sort of the way they talk about it is they're not worried too much about people raising the possibility
sentences.zh: 当行政官员谈论此事时，他们谈论的方式大概就是这样，他们不太担心人们提出

sentences.en: that we might go into recession because they think that's a sign people are taking the Fed seriously.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会陷入衰退的可能性，因为他们认为这是人们认真对待美联储的一个迹象。

sentences.en: And they hope there isn't a recession and they believe the Fed can pull this off without a recession.
sentences.zh: 他们希望不会发生经济衰退，并且相信美联储能够在没有经济衰退的情况下完成这一壮举。

sentences.en: Would it be fair, Jim, to say that if the president and his team had to choose, and it's not clear that they do have to choose, but if they had to choose,
sentences.zh: 吉姆，如果总统和他的团队必须做出选择（尽管目前尚不清楚他们是否必须做出选择），但如果他们非选不可的话，

sentences.en: given how worried they are about inflation, that they might prefer a lowercase r gentle recession that really solves the inflation problem in this country to a situation in which
sentences.zh: 鉴于他们对通胀的担忧程度，他们是否会更倾向于小写r的温和衰退（这确实解决了国内的通胀问题），而不是那种

sentences.en: there's no recession of any kind, but the terrible inflation we have right now stays in place?
sentences.zh: 没有任何形式的衰退，但我们现在面临的可怕通胀却依然存在的局面？

sentences.en: It's really hard to say which of those two,
sentences.zh: 这真的很难说这两者中哪一个，

sentences.en: I think that the White House would call those both kind of nightmare scenarios, they would prefer.
sentences.zh: 我认为白宫会把这两者都称为某种噩梦般的场景，他们会更倾向于……

sentences.en: But I will say this, they are very cognizant of the fact that for a lot of people, even though the economy does not appear right now to be in recession, for a lot of people,
sentences.zh: 但我得这么说，他们非常清楚这样一个事实：对许多人来说，尽管目前经济看起来并没有陷入衰退，但对许多人来说，

sentences.en: it feels very bad.
sentences.zh: 感觉非常糟糕。

sentences.en: They know that inflation is outpacing wage growth for a lot of people, which means they can just buy less, their dollars are going less far now.
sentences.zh: 他们知道通胀的增长速度超过了许多人的工资增长，这意味着他们能买的东西变少了，他们的钱现在不经花了。

sentences.en: And they know that's bad economically, they also know it's very bad politics for President Biden, so they would like to see that end.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这对经济不利，也知道这对拜登总统的政治前景非常不利，所以他们希望看到这种情况结束。

sentences.en: I mean, I think they would much rather see that end without a recession, because recessions do bad things for presidents too.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为他们更愿意看到这种情况在没有经济衰退的情况下结束，因为经济衰退对总统来说也不是什么好事。

sentences.en: But, you know, if the inflation we have just continues for several more years, I think it'd be very difficult for the president to be reelected.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果我们现在的通胀再持续好几年，我认为总统要连任将会非常困难。

sentences.en: Which might be an argument
sentences.zh: 这或许可以构成一个理由

sentences.en: for doing whatever it takes to lower inflation, even if it causes a recession.
sentences.zh: 为了降低通胀不惜一切代价，即使这会导致经济衰退。

sentences.en: This is a White House that still believes the Fed can bring inflation under control and the economy can keep growing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个仍然相信美联储能够控制通胀且经济能够继续增长的白宫。

sentences.en: It really believes that there does not have to be a recession, and so that is what they are trying to communicate to people in the economy in hopes that it comes true.
sentences.zh: 它坚信不一定非得发生经济衰退，因此这正是他们试图向经济中的人们传达的信息，希望它能成为现实。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, of course, the bear market that we're in, as you have told us, Jim, suggests that investors don't see it the way Biden does.
sentences.zh: 但当然，正如你所告诉我们的那样，吉姆，我们身处熊市表明投资者并不像拜登那样看待问题。

sentences.en: They think that lowering inflation almost by definition means hurting the economy and probably even sending us into a recession.
sentences.zh: 他们认为降低通胀几乎按定义就意味着伤害经济，甚至可能让我们陷入衰退。

sentences.en: The way I'd put it is investors see a higher chance of recession now than they thought a couple weeks ago, and they definitely seem to see a higher chance of recession
sentences.zh: 如果让我来表达的话，投资者现在看到经济衰退的可能性比几周前要高，而且他们看到的衰退可能性

sentences.en: than President Biden seems to right now.
sentences.zh: 绝对比拜登总统目前看到的要高。

sentences.en: What they are telling us with this bear market is that they don't see nearly the chance of avoiding recession or even that small R recession as maybe the White House
sentences.zh: 他们通过这个熊市向我们传达的信息是，他们并不认为像白宫此时所想的那样，

sentences.en: does at this point.
sentences.zh: 有那么大把握可以避免衰退，甚至连那种小R的衰退也觉得不太可能。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're worried about the big capital R recession.
sentences.zh: 他们担心的是那个大写R的严重衰退。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A bear market is a sign that the claws are swiping down to show us that that capital R recession may in fact be on the way.
sentences.zh: 熊市是一个信号，表明爪子正在向下抓挠，向我们展示大写R的经济衰退事实上可能正在路上。

sentences.en: I appreciate you somehow bringing it back to the claws, Jim.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，我很感激你不知怎么又把它扯回了爪子上。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: As always, we appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我们对此深表感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Later today, officials at the Federal Reserve are expected to announce a significant increase in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天晚些时候，美联储官员预计将宣布大幅提高美国

sentences.en: interest rate by as much as three quarters of a point in their latest and most forceful attempt so far to lower inflation.
sentences.zh: 利率，幅度高达四分之三点，这是他们迄今为止为降低通胀做出最新、最有力的尝试。

sentences.en: In interviews, economists told the Times that such a sharp hike increases the likelihood of a recession.
sentences.zh: 在采访中，经济学家告诉《时报》，如此急剧的加息增加了经济衰退的可能性。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the most powerful Republican in the Senate,
sentences.zh: 周二，参议院中最有权势的共和党人，

sentences.en: Minority Leader
sentences.zh: 少数党领袖

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, endorsed a bipartisan deal on a set of gun safety laws, paving the way for its passage.
sentences.zh: 来自肯塔基州的米奇·麦康奈尔，背书了一项关于一系列枪支安全法的两党协议，为该协议的通过铺平了道路。

sentences.en: For myself,
sentences.zh: 对我个人而言，

sentences.en: I'm comfortable with the framework and if the legislation ends up reflecting what the framework indicates,
sentences.zh: 我对这个框架感到满意，如果最终的立法反映了框架所表明的内容，

sentences.en: I'll be supportive.
sentences.zh: 我会给予支持。

sentences.en: Support from McConnell, a longtime defender of gun rights, is seen as a form of permission for the rest of the Senate's Republicans to eventually vote for the legislation,
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔作为枪支权利的长期捍卫者，他的支持被视为给参议院其余共和党人最终投票支持该立法的一种变相许可，

sentences.en: which would represent the most significant federal gun control measures in decades.
sentences.zh: 这将代表几十年来最重要的联邦枪支管制措施。

sentences.en: And,
sentences.zh: 并且，

sentences.en: Russian forces appear to be on the verge of seizing the strategically important city of Severodonetsk in eastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯军队似乎即将攻占乌克兰东部具有战略重要性的城市北顿涅茨克。

sentences.en: That would allow Russia to consolidate control of the region and claim a major victory after months of setbacks.
sentences.zh: 这将使俄罗斯能够巩固对该地区的控制，并在经历了数月的挫折后宣称取得重大胜利。

sentences.en: Russian forces have destroyed the last bridge that linked the city to Ukrainian-controlled territory, making it far harder for Ukrainian forces to defend.
sentences.zh: 俄军已经摧毁了连接该市与乌克兰控制领土的最后一座桥梁，这使得乌军防守变得难上加难。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rochelle Banja,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗谢尔·班贾（Rochelle Banja）制作，

sentences.en: Mooch Zaidi, and Eric Krupke, with help from Michael Simon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 穆奇·扎伊迪（Mooch Zaidi）和埃里克·克鲁普克（Eric Krupke）协助制作，迈克尔·西蒙·约翰逊（Michael Simon Johnson）提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George, with help from Michael Benoit, contains original music by Rowan Nemisto, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 节目由马克·乔治（Mark George）剪辑，迈克尔·贝努瓦（Michael Benoit）协助，原创音乐由罗恩·内米斯托（Rowan Nemisto）创作，音频工程由克里斯·伍德（Chris Wood）负责。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由旺德利（Wonderly）的吉姆·布伦伯格（Jim Brunberg）和本·兰斯福德（Ben Lansford）创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《电线切割机秀》中，我们正在为假期的节日招待做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让你的客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是遮光睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会晕过去来睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《电线切割机秀》。
